summary: Research on availability of David Platt's rigorous RH-verification code and Andrew Odlyzko's zeta computation resources

computational_code.description: Platt's rigorous zero-verification algorithm code is NOT publicly available as source code
details: Algorithm described in papers: arXiv:2004.09765 (2020), Mathematics of Computation 86(307) 2449-2467 (2017)
Reaches up to 3×10^12 (Platt-Trudgian 2020) and 30.6 billion (earlier work)
103+ billion zeros computed, with 2^-102 absolute precision per zero
Completeness verified using rigorous version of Turing's method
evidence: Papers published in peer-reviewed venues describe algorithm but no code release
arXiv papers (2004.09765, related work) have no ancillary files or code links
No GitHub repository under David Platt's name for zeta verification code
LMFDB references data acquisition but no mention of open-source algorithm implementation

computed_zeros_data.description: Pre-computed zero data is publicly available through LMFDB
computed_zeros_data.format: Binary indexed format with Python wrapper (platt_zeros.py)

computation_code.notes: Odlyzko developed the Odlyzko-Schönhage algorithm (1988) but no public source code release found. Algorithm described in papers only.

data_files.zeros_lmfdb_2Mto20M: LMFDB zeros from 2M to 20M range (229 MB)

project_current_state.gap_to_platt_record: Heights 20M to 30.6B (30.6 billion) not currently stored
